o1.biggest_strength: It reads the pilot correctly: Controllers/Heads of Finance at 50-300 person SaaS companies, timed to pricing-page changes, with no links in step 1 and a grounded reply-rate forecast.
o1.biggest_mistake: The copy leans a little too much on reply-keyword asks like “reply yes” and “reply steps,” which feels more like a sales sequence than a finance peer-to-peer note.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the CTAs so each email has one natural finance-person ask, move the proof out of step 1 or make it less prominent, and avoid depending on a one-page summary/three-step asset that was not provided.

o2.biggest_strength: The email copy sounds the most like a finance person writing to another finance person: specific, plain, and tied to pricing changes, rev rec, close, audit timing and engineering ownership.
o2.biggest_mistake: The reply-rate forecast is a little optimistic with the 7%-10% range and the 1.25x assumption; I would rather anchor closer to 6.8%-7.9% until tested.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the forecast more conservative, add slightly clearer one-ask CTAs in steps 1 and 4, and keep the meeting ask in step 2 a touch softer.

reason: Both got the strategy right, but I would rather put Output 2 in front of customers because the copy feels more natural, less gimmicky, and more on-brand. Output 1 has slightly better list math, but its reply-keyword CTAs need more editing before I would send it.
